title: Grateful Dead Live at Springer's Inn Portland on 1970-01-16
source: Source: sbd > reel master > reel > pcm (sony beta tape ESX-HiFi/L-750) - Given to Tim Dalton by the late Harvey Lubar; Transfer: pcm > Sony SL-10 > Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch Pro > Tascam DA-3000 (WAV 16-bit/44.1k) - transferred by Charlie Miller; Lineage: wav > iZotope RX6 Advanced > iZotope 5 Advanced > CD Wave > TLH > Flac 16; edited and mastered SIRMick February 2018

ai_review.summary: Rough but solid early‑70 soundboard capture highlighted by a fiery China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is a typical early‑70 tape – a bit rough around the edges but still listenable, coming from a soundboard source. Musically the show shines, especially with Jerry digging into the new China>Rider transition, and fans note this period as “primo Dead.” The only downside mentioned is the absence of an Easy Wind jam.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews are uniformly positive about the performance and give a decent (though rough) impression of the recording; weighting show quality higher yields a rating just above four stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early‑70 tape sounds a bit rough with typical hiss and occasional muddiness, but remains clear enough to enjoy the music.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical early‑70 set with a raw edge; transitions flow well, especially the highlighted China>Rider segment.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Really digging the new China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider sequence.
